data.body:
## c379 triaged: a genuine defect that an ACCEPTED ADR already settled the other way

Classification: genuine defect, reproducible on current origin/main (7d3907101dd6), not fixed since
filing. Fix agent dispatched.

MECHANISM -- a dead conjunct. next_batch.py:262 already excludes every structural container via
parent_ids_with_children (built at :162). The branch at :264-267 guards on
'ttype == "story" and tid not in parent_ids_with_children', whose SECOND CONJUNCT IS DEAD because
line 262 guarantees it. So it reduces to 'type == story => never schedulable'. Worse, the rendered
reason at :405-407 -- 'needs implementation planning (story has 0 children)' -- asserts an inference
nothing verifies: the branch never consults plan-review state, so a childless story holding a current
CERTIFIED plan-review PASS still reports as unplanned.

The asymmetry is the clean falsification: under one epic, a childless EPIC is batched and a childless
BUG is batched; only a childless STORY is vetoed. Whatever 'stories are containers' would mean, it
cannot survive a childless epic being schedulable.

THE PROJECT ALREADY DECIDED THIS. docs/adr/0078-plan-review-container-leaf-scrutiny.md (Accepted):
'Proportionate scrutiny is keyed on container (has children) vs leaf (no children), NEVER on ticket
type... the defect is that TYPE is a poor proxy for ALTITUDE: a childless epic behaves like a leaf, a
story with children like a container.' ADR 0078 fixed it in plan-review (bug a278) and it was never
propagated to the scheduler. The same rule is restated in the shipped author guide, in
plan_review/registry.py, det_floor.py and docs/plan-review-gate.md. The branch itself was inherited
verbatim from the bash->Python port (92caa823ae17), not introduced by any decision.

THIRD INSTANCE TODAY OF THE SAME META-PATTERN: a decision or guard that exists but does not
propagate. (1) 740d -- ticket 3476 fixed the bare-repo class and left a hand-maintained 3-file
allowlist, so a file added four days later reintroduced it silently. (2) The ADR 0110/0111 collisions
-- the .numbers reservation marker is only created at authoring time, so any plan reading the highest
number is stale by landing. (3) c379 -- ADR 0078 settled container-vs-type and the scheduler never
heard about it. Worth watching for; the fixes that stick are the ones derived from the tree rather
than hand-registered.

COST EVIDENCE, and it is the part that makes this more than cosmetic: multiple tickets were RETYPED
from story to task to route around the veto -- indigoid-unmystic-serpent,
truthful-specified-silverfish, immune-floury-toad all carry the note 'Retyped from story to task after
the final scheduling audit: next-batch intentionally skips childless stories as planning containers',
and forcible-diminished-lamb (08ab) is now type task as a result. Agent commentary INFERRED FROM THE
BUG became the only text defending the behavior. That is a nice cautionary case: observed behavior
got written up as intent, and the writeup then looked like prior art.

PARITY GAP between operations, not surfaces: all three surfaces (CLI reads_cli.py:561, library
_reads.py:204, MCP _mcp_reads.py:442) funnel through one compute, so one fix covers them. But
reads.ready_states (reads.py:560) applies no type filter, so 'ready' returns the childless story that
'next-batch' skips -- two operations documented as a single pipeline disagreeing about one ticket.
AC4 closes it.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED not estimated: removing lines 264-267 and running all 23 test files that
mention next-batch gives '1 failed, 405 passed', and the single failure is
test_next_batch_behavior.py::test_childless_story_needs_planning -- i.e. the test that CODIFIES the
bug. Removing a branch also lowers cyclomatic complexity, so the ratchet reports stale and passes,
and no mechanism is added.

Deliberately left out of scope, recorded for a follow-up ticket: after the fix
skipped_needs_planning can never be non-empty. Retention is right for compatibility
(_mcp_models.py:250, next_batch.schema.json:29), but a permanently-empty field is small maintenance
debt.
